title: Convergence of Hermite degree truncations
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ belong to $L^2$ for the product of $n$ standard Gaussian measures. For each natural number $k$, form the sum over multi-indices whose coordinates are at most $k$, retaining only those of total degree at most $k$, with each term the Hermite coefficient of $f$ times the corresponding normalized multivariate Hermite function. The $L^2$ distance between $f$ and this sum tends to zero as $k\to\infty$.
hypotheses_covered: The dimension $n$ is a natural number, with no further restriction.
The function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ belongs to $L^2$ for the product standard Gaussian measure.
